newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan leaders mourn Chiang Kai-shek's grandson.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan leaders mourn Chiang Kai-shek's grandson.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui mourned the death of Chiang Hsiao-yung, grandson of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, at his funeral on Sunday, although Chiang Hsiao-yung had been a critic of Lee.

Other ranking government officials also attended the funeral. State-funded television showed the coffin covered with the flags of Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party and the Republic of China government.
Chiang Hsiao-yung, who died in late December at 48 from cancer of the oesophagus, was the son of late president Chiang Ching-kuo.

Chiang Kai-shek and later Chiang Ching-kuo ruled Taiwan with supreme authority after taking refuge on the island in 1949 following the Chinese Nationalists' civil war defeat on the mainland at the hands of the communists.
The Chiang family's influence started to fade when Chiang Ching-kuo started democratic reforms before his death in 1988.
Despite his family background, Chiang Hsiao-yung did not play an active role in Taiwanese politics. He worked for several Nationalist Party-owned businesses before moving abroad.
Chiang Hsiao-yung's half-brother, Foreign Minister John Chang who bears the surname of his mother, is the only Chiang family member still holding a high government position.
